newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain banks' interest income to fall further-study.
newsitem.headline: Spain banks' interest income to fall further-study.

text.p: Spanish banks' net interest income will continue to fall this year, albeit at a lower rate than in 1996, industry association AEB said on Monday.
Overall, Spanish banks expect to see profit rise moderately in 1997 due to healthy results from own-account trading and the continued fall in bad debts.
In 1996, average net interest income over total assets fell to 2.20 percent from four percent in 1991, in line with the average in Europe.
"The fall (in net interest income) will continue but at a lower rate than in 1996," Julio Rodriguez, analyst at AEB told a press conference.
Although short-term interest rates were likely to fall further this year, this was unlikely to pose such a problem as interest margins had already narrowed dramatically, he said.
Conversely, expectations of lower interest rates could prompt banks to boost own-account trading, at least partly compensating for the fall in net interest income, as was the case last year.
In 1996. overall profit on own-account trading rose 64.6 percent to 200 billion pesetas.
Another issue set to limit the fall in net interest income was a likely pick up in economic activity which should boost loan demand.
The banking sector should also be helped by the fall in the deposit guarantee fund, that as of today has been reduced to one per thousand from two per thousand.
This is expected to free around 22 billion pesetas of liquidity.
Rodriguez said that the lower payments to back deposits is due to better banking conditions after the highly expensive overhaul of Banco Espanol de Credito (Banesto).
